title: Hardwood Over a Crawlspace: Vapor Barriers and Moisture Rules for Kirkland Homes

blocks.lead: Hardwood over a crawlspace works when three things are true: the crawlspace floor is covered with a sealed 6-mil vapor barrier, the plywood subfloor meters at 12 percent moisture or less and within 4 points of the new flooring, and a moisture retarder goes between subfloor and boards.
blocks.detail: Miss any one of those and the floor cups within a year. Kirkland's lakeside water table and wet winters make crawlspaces here damper than most. Wills Flooring installs hardwood at $3.25 per sq ft; crawlspace barrier work and subfloor prep are quoted at the free estimate.

blocks.html: Most Kirkland houses from the 1960s through the 1990s in Juanita, Finn Hill, Rose Hill and Bridle Trails sit on a crawlspace, and the closer you get to Lake Washington the wetter that crawlspace is. We get called to look at cupped hardwood every winter, and the story is nearly always the same: nice floor, correct installation, nobody looked under the house. This post is the checklist we run before a single board goes down over a Kirkland crawlspace.

blocks.text: What a damp crawlspace does to a hardwood floor

items.title: Cupping
items.text: Moisture comes up through the subfloor and into the bottom of each board. The bottom swells, the top does not, and every board edge rises. Cupping across a whole room is almost always a crawlspace problem, not a spill.

items.title: Crowning after a bad fix
items.text: If a cupped floor is sanded flat while still wet, it dries later and the centers hump up. The floor is then too thin to sand again. Drying first is the whole game.

items.title: Gaps and squeaks
items.text: A floor that took on crawlspace moisture in winter shrinks hard in summer. The result is wide seasonal gaps and loosened fasteners that squeak, even though the boards were fine when installed.

items.title: Mold and finish failure
items.text: Persistent moisture under the boards grows mold on the plywood and can lift the finish from below. By the time it smells musty in the living room, the subfloor usually needs replacing.

blocks.text: The moisture rules we install by

head: Check
Target
If it fails
rows: 6-mil or thicker polyethylene over 100 percent of the soil, seams overlapped 12 in and taped, run up the stem walls
Install or repair the barrier first; this is quoted with the job or handled by your crawlspace contractor
Dry to the touch, no pooling, downspouts carrying water away from the house
Fix drainage before flooring. No barrier survives standing water
12 percent or less on a pin meter, checked in at least 20 spots across the floor
Dehumidify and re-test in a week or two; do not install
Within 4 points for strip flooring, within 2 points for planks over 3 in wide
Keep acclimating the flooring in the house until it matches
Below about 60 percent, with working vents or a conditioned, encapsulated space
Add ventilation, a dehumidifier or encapsulation before installation
15-lb asphalt felt or a rated underlayment paper over the whole subfloor for nail-down
Never install nail-down solid hardwood directly on bare plywood over a crawlspace
blocks.note: These are the manufacturer and NWFA-style requirements every warranty depends on. We meter and write the readings on the quote so you have them.

blocks.text: What happens before the first board

items.text: We open the crawlspace hatch. We look for the barrier, standing water, insulation falling off the joists, and mold on the underside of the subfloor. We meter the plywood from above in every room.

If the ground cover is missing or torn, it gets replaced with sealed 6-mil poly run up the stem walls. Downspouts that dump next to the foundation get extensions. This is often a week or two before flooring.
A subfloor over 12 percent gets a dehumidifier and fans, then a re-test. Kirkland winter readings of 14 to 16 percent are common and usually come down within two weeks once the barrier is in.
items.note: We will not install on a wet subfloor even if the schedule says so. The warranty is worth more than the calendar.

items.text: Flooring is delivered into the house, out of the boxes, in the rooms where it will go, until its moisture content is within 4 points of the subfloor. Typically 5 to 10 days in Kirkland.
Felt or rated paper goes down over the whole subfloor, then the boards are nailed or glued. Readings from every stage go on your paperwork.

blocks.text: Solid or engineered over a Kirkland crawlspace?

a.title: The safer choice when
items: The crawlspace has a history of dampness even after barrier work
You want planks over 5 in wide, which move most with moisture
The home is near the lake in Juanita, Houghton or along Lake Washington Blvd
You want glue-down with a moisture-cure adhesive that doubles as a vapor retarder

b.title: Works well when
items: The crawlspace is dry, sealed and metered below 12 percent
You want a floor that can be refinished many times over decades
Boards are 2 1/4 to 4 in strip, which tolerates small humidity swings
The house stays heated and humidity-controlled year-round

blocks.title: When we say no:
blocks.text: If there is standing water in the crawlspace, active mold on the subfloor, or the plywood meters above 16 percent and will not come down, we do not install hardwood that season. We will quote the crawlspace fix and come back, or talk about vinyl plank for that room if the moisture cannot be controlled.
Mistakes that cup a new floor within a year

items.html: Skipping the crawlspace visit. A crew that quotes from the living room has no idea what is under the house. Ask if they opened the hatch.
Barrier that covers 80 percent of the soil. Moisture finds the bare 20 percent. Full coverage with taped seams or it is not a barrier.
Acclimating in the garage. Kirkland garages in January are close to outdoor humidity. Flooring acclimates in the rooms it will live in, with the heat on.
Installing on a single meter reading. One dry spot near the furnace says nothing about the corner over the wettest soil. Twenty readings, worst one counts.
Nailing solid hardwood to bare plywood. The felt layer is cheap and it is the last line of defense. No retarder, no warranty.
Closing the vents for winter and forgetting. Sealed vents trap crawlspace moisture all spring. Either encapsulate and dehumidify properly or leave the vents working.

blocks.text: Checklist before hardwood goes over your crawlspace

items: Open the crawlspace hatch and look: barrier present and intact, soil dry, no puddles, no musty smell
Check that downspouts and grading move water away from the foundation, especially on the uphill side of Finn Hill and Rose Hill lots
Ask for subfloor moisture readings in writing, at least 20 spots, before delivery
Confirm the flooring will acclimate inside the house until it is within 4 points of the subfloor
Confirm a moisture retarder is included under nail-down floors
If the crawlspace has a history, lean engineered and consider a dehumidifier below
Read how long hardwood needs to acclimate so the delivery date fits the plan

faq.q: Do I need a vapor barrier in the crawlspace before installing hardwood?
faq.a: Yes. A 6-mil or heavier polyethylene ground cover over all of the soil, seams overlapped and taped, is the first requirement. Without it, ground moisture rises through the subfloor into the boards and the floor cups. It is separate from the felt or paper retarder installed under the flooring itself.

faq.q: What moisture content should a subfloor be before hardwood?
faq.a: 12 percent or less on a pin meter, and within 4 percentage points of the new flooring for strip boards, within 2 points for planks wider than 3 in. We take at least 20 readings across the floor and go by the worst one, not the average.

faq.q: Is engineered hardwood better than solid over a crawlspace?
faq.a: It is more forgiving. The cross-ply core moves less with humidity, and glue-down engineered can use an adhesive that also blocks vapor. Solid strip hardwood works well too if the crawlspace is sealed and dry. Wide solid planks are the riskiest option over a Kirkland crawlspace.

faq.q: How long does hardwood need to acclimate in a Kirkland home?
faq.a: Until it matches the subfloor, not a fixed number of days. In practice that is 5 to 10 days inside the heated house, boxes opened, in the rooms where it will be installed. We meter both the flooring and the subfloor and start only when they are within range.

faq.q: Why is my hardwood floor cupping in winter?
faq.a: Usually crawlspace moisture. Wet winter soil raises the humidity under the house, the subfloor absorbs it, and the bottom of each board swells more than the top. Fixing the barrier and drainage, then letting the floor dry for weeks, often flattens it. Sand only after it is dry and stable.
